newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian Bank cuts prime 1.5 points to 14.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: Indian Bank cuts prime 1.5 points to 14.0 pct.

text.p: State-owned Indian Bank has cut its prime lending rate (PLR) to 14.0 percent from 15.5 percent, effective April 16, a senior bank official said on Friday.
State Bank of India, the country's largest commercial bank, cut its PLR to 14 percent from 14.5 on Tuesday, hours after the Reserve Bank of India announced its credit policy for 1997/98.
The SBI's move was followed by a series of cuts in PLR by other Indian banks.
The prime rate is the interest banks charge on loans to their blue-chip clients. Other companies have to pay a higher rate on bank loans.
Indian Bank's maximum spread between the prime rate and the highest rate is 4.0 percentage points, the official told Reuters from his Madras headquarters in southern Tamil Nadu.
